citations.claim: energy just before collision is below initial, no violation
first energy_bound violation — energy ~4.5x initial, exceeds 3652 allowed
body 1 speed more than doubles across the colliding step, showing spurious kinetic gain

counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 0.9 to 0 (single field). With lower restitution the spurious energy gain disappears and energy stays below initial (2312 J), so energy_bound no longer violated. Proves restitution handling in the collision impulse is the cause.

explanation: Shrunk scenario shows deterministic energy explosion at first body-body collision with controller disabled (work 0) and no walls. At step 8 energy is ~3125 J (below E0 3316 J) and bodies are separated; at step 9 they are touching (gap 0.047) after 42 substeps and total energy jumps to 14969 J (~4.5x), exceeding allowed 3652 J. Body 1 speed more than doubles from 22.8 to 64.3 m/s in one step, showing spurious kinetic gain. High restitution (0.9/1.0) with high closing speed causes impulse + positional correction to add energy instead of conserving/dissipating.
vision_note: Steps 6 to 8 show two blue circles drifting down-left together with a slowly shrinking gap but remaining clearly separated. At step 9 they are in touching/near-overlapping contact at the lower-center with no visible walls, waypoints, or explosive separation in that single frame.
